title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
claim: Polyalcohols and related O-donor ligands, previously little used for this purpose, can support high-nuclearity lanthanide and 4f–3d hydroxide clusters under hydro/solvothermal conditions, and the ligand present in the product may be generated in situ from a polyalcohol precursor.
explanation: Examples include myo-inositol/cyclohexanetriol clusters Dy24Mn2 and double-cage Ln37, TEOA with acetate in Gd12Fe14, GlcNAc dehydration to Chromogen I in nonanuclear Ln9, and N-methyldiethanolamine in Dy72. The transferable point is that this ligand class is viable, not a single nuclearity rule.
scope: Hydroxide clusters of lanthanides, including heterometallic Mn, Fe, and related ions, supported by polyalcohols or amine-bisalcohol derivatives.
conditions: Hydro/solvothermal heating; ligands may be used as supplied or transformed during the reaction.
caveats: Most outcomes are individual isolations; ligand transformation (for example GlcNAc to Chromogen I) is case-specific and not a general requirement.
